app/package.json:13-14 — direct deps on @lit-labs/ssr ^4.0.0 and @lit-labs/ssr-client ^1.1.8; Lit Labs packages are officially 'pre-release software' (lit.dev/docs/libraries/labs/)
app/package.json:21 — typescript ^7.0.2, the native-Go major released Jul 8, 2026 (~3.5 months old, recently-stable)

reach.rationale: Every central feature (routing, SSR, server adapter, build) sits on a self-described-alpha framework plus a Lit Labs SSR engine, and dev tooling includes the 3-month-old TypeScript 7.0 — more than 'one or two recently-stable APIs'. It stays off flags, canaries and add-ons, and stays on the current stable releases, which keeps this from being a 5.

evidence: app/src/routes/(home).client.ts:3 and app/src/routes/pokemon/[name].client.ts:1 — client scripts import no Gracile APIs at all, so the riskiest client-side tier is untouched
app/src/lib/api.ts:21-22 — the custom POKEDEX_BUILD_STEP build-phase flag is centralized in one isBuildStep() helper
app/document shell: app/src/document.ts — single document factory; app/server.js:14-24 — single server file uses the official node adapter exports
app/package.json:12 — exact version pin '0.11.0' (no caret) isolates against alpha-era minor breaking changes

containment.rationale: Platform reliance cannot be contained by definition, but the app does everything reasonable: it deliberately avoids the unstable client tiers (hydration/islands/client-router) in favor of plain stable Lit, centralizes its one homegrown flag behind a helper, and pins the framework exactly.

evidence: app/vite.config.ts:10 — output: 'server' is required by the spec's request-time-data rule; no stable alternative exists within the mandated framework
app/package.json:13 — @lit-labs/ssr is Gracile's engine requirement (@gracile/engine peer-depends on it), not a free choice
app/package.json:14 — @lit-labs/ssr-client is declared but never used: no hydration import anywhere and zero Lit elements, an unjustified experimental-tier dependency
app/package.json:21 — TypeScript 7.0 adopted shortly after release buys ~10x faster type-checks (devblogs.microsoft.com) but is optional novelty over TS 6.x for this small codebase
app/src/routes/api/species-index.ts:9 — Response.json endpoint via the documented method-map handler; spec requirement with no stable-API downside
justification.rationale: Every experimental-tier choice is either spec-mandated or buys concrete value, and the genuinely risky framework tiers were swapped for long-stable Lit in the browser. The unused @lit-labs/ssr-client dependency and the just-because adoption of the brand-new TS 7 major keep this from a 5.

findings.issue: @lit-labs/ssr-client (hydration helper) is declared as a direct dependency but the app never hydrates: no '@gracile/gracile/hydration' import and zero Lit custom elements, and @gracile/client already provides it transitively
findings.suggestion: Drop @lit-labs/ssr-client from dependencies; keep @lit-labs/ssr only if a Gracile package actually requires it as a peer from the host (otherwise let @gracile/gracile supply it)

findings.issue: The whole app depends on Gracile 0.11.0, which the project's own current docs label 'alpha state'; pre-1.0 minors can carry breaking changes
findings.suggestion: Keep the exact version pin (already done) and treat upgrades as reviewed, breaking-change events; consider a thin wrapper around route/document helpers if the codebase is owned for years

findings.issue: typescript ^7.0.2 — TypeScript 7.0 went stable only on 2026-07-08, a brand-new major adopted inside its first quarter
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep given Microsoft's compatibility statements and the large DX payoff, but TS 6.x is the conservative choice if CI stability matters more than check speed

findings.issue: Custom POKEDEX_BUILD_STEP environment flag couples the Vite build config to route handlers (checked in 7 route files via isBuildStep), a homegrown stand-in for a framework-provided build-phase signal
findings.suggestion: Keep the isBuildStep() helper as the single choke point (it already is), and watch for an official Gracile build-phase API to replace the env var

summary: The app runs entirely on an alpha-status platform (Gracile 0.11.0, current stable release, exact-pinned) with Lit Labs SSR in its supply chain, and adopts the 3-month-old TypeScript 7 for dev tooling — so baseline experimental exposure is high but largely mandated by the spec. Inside that constraint it makes consistently conservative choices: zero experimental flags, no hydration/islands/client-router add-ons, and client scripts built purely on long-stable Lit and DOM APIs, which would survive a framework swap. The only gratuitous item is an unused @lit-labs/ssr-client dependency.
